quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. Children are playing nearby. What should you do before you move your car?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children can hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When backing up, look through your back window for people and obstacles. Do not rely only on mirrors. Get out of the vehicle and check behind it before backing into or out of a driveway.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors for traffic behind you?

options.text: Every 45 seconds
Every 20 seconds
Every 10 seconds
Every 6 to 8 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 6 to 8 seconds
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every 6 to 8 seconds. This helps you know if someone is following too closely or coming up too fast. It also helps you know how much space is behind your car.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far your vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your car?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects your stopping ability. Reduce your speed when roads are poor or slippery to keep control of your vehicle and avoid skidding.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as traffic flow.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic nearest to them.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than large vehicles.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They may move faster and have less noticeable lights. Stay alert to prevent collisions with these smaller road users.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: When passing traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines may be crossed, but solid lines may not. You can cross solid yellow lines only when turning.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning when driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at the speed you would use in ideal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast in wet conditions, your tires lose contact with the road. Your car rides on top of the water, called hydroplaning. Driving slowly in rain prevents this.

questions.question: If a car ahead is using high beams, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road if an oncoming car has bright headlights. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your course until the car passes.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign do?

options.text: Can be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.
Has a triangular shape.
Is blue with black lettering.
Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Curve and turn warning signs often have a recommended speed sign attached. This sign shows a safe speed for driving through curves and turns. Never drive faster than this speed, especially in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycles is true?

options.text: It is okay for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two people is more balanced than a motorcycle with one rider.
You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
You can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full width of a lane. Make sure your entire vehicle is in the left lane before you pass a motorcycle.

questions.question: You see this sign for a railroad crossing with no signal. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep the same speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains and be ready to stop if you see or hear one. Never try to drive faster than an oncoming train.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines. When can you cross them?

options.text: Only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
Only to pass other vehicles if no traffic is coming.
Never.
Only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass in either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: A round sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead. This sign is placed a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When driving in thick fog with very poor visibility, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at under 10 miles per hour.
Use your high beam headlights.
Pull off the road and stop with your emergency flashers on.
Honk your horn every few seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and stop with your emergency flashers on.
questions.explanation: If fog becomes so thick that you cannot see, pull off the road safely. Turn on your emergency flashers and stop. Wait until visibility gets better before you drive again.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. In this case, the road curves left. There may be several of these signs placed along the curve.

questions.question: It is unlawful for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Two motorcycles can share a lane, but a car should never share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens, move as far right as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. Do this no matter which direction the vehicle is coming from.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A stop sign is ahead.
Side road.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should look for a gap of ____ seconds.

options.text: One to two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Look for a four-second gap before changing lanes. This gap gives you and the car behind you each two seconds of space when you merge.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: To turn left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the centerline. Start your turn just before you reach the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: When can you park in an access aisle next to a handicap spot?

options.text: Never.
When you have a disability plate or placard.
When all other spaces are full.
When you park for just a few minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot park in an access aisle. Parking there is illegal and can result in a fine of at least $200.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping:

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on loose gravel or stone surfaces.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: So you can see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers try to pass large vehicles before pulling behind them.
Because following too closely will pull you into the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles can block the driver's view of you. They also block your view of the road ahead. Increase your following distance so you can see around the sides and see the road in front of you.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front is disabled.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you do so safely and without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After you complete the turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the right lane.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish your turn in the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: When you must stop at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, you should:

options.text: Not stop.
Slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet on each side, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can see traffic clearly before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see traffic clearly before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop at the point nearest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: When entering a short interstate ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Enter the far-right lane right away and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to get up to traffic speed.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic before speeding up. Usually, stay stopped while waiting for the gap to appear.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get drivers to let you through.
Drive around the back of a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Stay farther back from the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop if the car suddenly stops. Use your headlights correctly at night, switching between high and low beams as needed.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop completely, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down to a safe speed and cross the intersection carefully.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens out your car.

questions.question: You should stay farther back from the car ahead when you:

options.text: Are following a small passenger vehicle.
Are being tailgated by another driver.
Are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are being tailgated by another driver.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space in front of your car and do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a crash.

questions.question: If you cannot see clearly to the sides at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see cross traffic clearly, stop and move forward slowly until you can see both directions.

questions.question: Highways and roads freeze before ramps and bridges.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges freeze before highways because they are in the air and lose heat faster. Drive slowly and carefully when crossing bridges in cold weather.

questions.question: Round signs tell you about:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you that a railroad crossing is coming. Be very careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: This sign shows a type of:

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and get ready to yield or stop before turning.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Turn right after you stop completely.
Right turns are not allowed.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: Signs like this show rules you must always follow. This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: In bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination quickly.
Stay closer to the car ahead.
Stay farther from the car ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: In wet weather, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when it is safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:

options.text: Stop, look for other cars, then go if the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells drivers to slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to:

options.text: Other cars also turning left.
All cars coming toward you.
People on the sidewalk waiting to walk.

questions.correctAnswerText: All cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicycles, and other vehicles with the right-of-way.

questions.question: When slowing down where other drivers may not expect it, you should:

options.text: Hit the brakes hard.
Release the accelerator and coast to a stop.
Tap your brakes three or four times quickly to warn drivers.
Honk your horn to warn drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes three or four times quickly to warn drivers.
questions.explanation: Tap your brakes three or four times quickly before slowing down. This makes your brake lights flash and alerts other drivers to your intentions.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a crosswalk.

options.text: 15 feet
10 feet
5 feet
1 foot

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 feet
questions.explanation: Parking is not allowed within 15 feet of a crosswalk.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep scanning ahead for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep scanning ahead for hazards.
questions.explanation: Drive defensively by looking ahead for dangers. Scan the road around you constantly. Do not stare only at the car in front of you.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Removes the effects of alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or reduce alcohol in your system.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign travel at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: The most important thing to remember about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: When driving through curves, your vehicle's weight pulls outward. To stay in control, you must slow down before entering the curve.

questions.question: When driving in fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
Other drivers might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights bounce back at your eyes. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Let oncoming vehicles go first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic gets a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming vehicles go first.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must allow pedestrians and oncoming traffic to go first.

questions.question: A "No standing" sign means:

options.text: You cannot stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if the driver stays in the car.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload items.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you may only stop for a short time to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: It is safe to use cruise control on snowy or icy roads if you reduce your speed.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads. Your tires may lose grip and you will lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Watch for pedestrians crossing.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells you that construction work is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic signs in the work zone.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. You must obey all regulatory signs.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always expect vehicles to stop for you in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop for you.
Use crosswalks only when convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way, a vehicle that is too close may not be able to stop.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow center line. This tells you:

options.text: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
Traffic moves in one direction only.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe.
